issue.title: Model/pool-alias resolution silently falls back to launch-default model, breaking 6 tests in test_workflow_executor.py and test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py
issue.description:
Six tests across two files fail deterministically on master, unrelated to any
in-progress epic, with a shared root cause: model/provider resolution silently
falls back to the launch-default model instead of honoring `%model:` directives,
pooled-alias cursor state, or gh-wrapper provenance.

Failing node IDs (all reproduce standalone with `-p no:randomly`, not just under
the full parallel suite):

- tests/test_workflow_executor.py::TestShouldHitl::test_inherited_model_override_beats_step_model_directive
  (`%model:pro` on a workflow step is ignored; `directives.model` comes back
  `'sonnet'` instead of the inherited `'gemini-3-flash-preview'` override)
- tests/test_workflow_executor.py::TestShouldHitl::test_prompt_step_chat_history_includes_step_metadata
  (`metadata_model` comes back `'sonnet'` instead of `'o3'`)
- tests/test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py::test_two_consecutive_default_launches_alternate_pool_members
  (pool cursor never advances; both launches select the same member)
- tests/test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py::test_explicit_large_directive_and_default_alias_share_pool_cursor
  (same symptom: selected member does not match the frozen pool cursor)
- tests/test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py::test_root_metadata_step_marker_and_chat_agree_with_invoked_model
  (`agent_meta.json` is missing the `model_alias_trail` key entirely --
  `KeyError: 'model_alias_trail'`, not merely a wrong value)
- tests/test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py::test_root_metadata_reconciles_after_gh_wrapper_display_rename
  (wrong provider entirely: `('claude', 'sonnet')` instead of the expected
  `('codex', 'gpt-5.6-sol')`)

Likely area: the pooled/size-alias launch-selection and provenance-recording
machinery built by epics sase-mf ("Simplify built-in model routing", phase
sase-mf.2 commit 2fcca46eb "feat!: replace role model aliases with size launch
settings") and sase-n8 ("Agent history for a model alias in Launch Control",
phase sase-n8.1 "Record the alias resolution trail and its origin at launch",
commit 96b48d0ab), plus follow-up 9568dd475 "fix: preserve anonymous workflow
attribution after rename" -- all closed 2026-08-15/16. Task sase-ks ("Thread
authoritative load-balanced alias selections into follow-up metadata") covered
an adjacent but distinct race-condition symptom in the same subsystem and was
closed 2026-08-14 as "superseded in substance" by commit 9df15dbe2; these
failures suggest that reconciliation has since regressed, but the exact
defect differs from sase-ks's race-condition framing (these fail
deterministically, single-threaded, with no concurrent cursor movement), so
this is filed as a new, related task rather than a +1 on sase-ks.

Discovered while landing epic sase-pq (task-type gate presentation) during
`just check-full`/`just test-cost` verification.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake:
Reproduces deterministically, not intermittently: ran each failing node twice
in isolation with `-p no:randomly` (disabling pytest-randomly reordering) and
got the identical wrong value both times -- e.g.
test_inherited_model_override_beats_step_model_directive always resolves
`'sonnet'` instead of `'gemini-3-flash-preview'`, never intermittently
succeeding. Also reproduced identically at commit 3df5c321b4 (the commit
immediately preceding epic sase-pq's first commit, i.e. before sase-pq
started, in a separate worktree sharing this checkout's .venv), ruling out
both test-order pollution from the full parallel suite and any sase-pq change
as the cause.
